inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash flow statement, Stock compensation expense $83M (FY0 base). ADM publishes no combined SBC-plus-withholding-tax figure, so this is the cash-flow add-back only. 9M-2026 expense was $176M vs $93M in 9M-2025 (Q3 2026 10-Q cash flow statement), which is what the forward sbc_pct_path is anchored to.
inputs.wacc_rationale: 8.7% on USD flows, identical in all three scenarios: ~4.2% 10yr UST plus ~4.5pp equity premium, blended with BBB-range debt. Cyclicality and policy risk are carried in the scenario flows and the weights, not in per-scenario discount rates (owner-fcf-adaptations rule f). The prior build ran 8.2/8.7/9.5 by scenario; that spread is removed.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment B: US GAAP operating lease cost is already expensed inside EBITDA, so no separate lease line and lease liabilities are excluded from net debt.
inputs.nci_treatment: Immaterial (non-controlling interests in equity are single-digit millions); attributable earnings used as reported, no bridge deduction.
inputs.notes: UPDATE of the 2026-09-25 build. Model: owner-FCF component DCF (operating company, cyclical commodity processor), same route as the prior valuation, with owner-fcf-adaptations rule (f): risk charged once, in mid-cycle-normalised flows. FY0 stays FY2025 (last audited year), so year 1 is FY2026, which is now three quarters reported. REFRESHED: price, net debt and share count to the 30 Sep 2026 balance sheet; buyback pace; FY2026 guidance (adjusted EPS raised to ~5.50-5.80, capex cut to 1.2-1.3B). RE-JUDGED: (1) year-1 growth, margin, capex, D&A in all three scenarios, to 9M-2026 actuals plus guidance (9M revenue 65.5B, 9M adjusted EBITDA 3.81B; FY2026 lands near 86.5B revenue and 5.1B EBITDA); (2) year-2 growth, because the FY2026 revenue step-up is price not volume (the 10-Q attributes +5.0B to higher sales prices against lower volumes), so base holds revenue flat in year 2 to keep through-cycle EBITDA dollars where the prior build had them rather than capitalising a 5% margin on a price-inflated base; (3) the SBC path, since 0.10% of revenue was anchored to the FY2025 trough-year expense and the 9M-2026 run-rate is about double; (4) methodology: one WACC, one terminal growth and one terminal cap for all scenarios, and the cap raised from 8/10/12x to 12x. The prior 10x was justified by ADM rarely trading above 12-14x EV/EBITDA, but the cap applies to terminal FCF, not EBITDA; 12x terminal FCF is the bottom of the method range for cyclicals and still only about 5.7x terminal EBITDA. DELIBERATELY UNCHANGED: base margin path from year 2 on (5.4 falling to 5.0%); management said crush and biofuel margins may have peaked while staying historically strong into 2027, which is what the path already assumes. A quantified FY2027 guide, or an EPA/45Z rule change, would move it. Cash tax path (20 rising to 23%; 9M-2026 effective rate 17.3% is consistent with a 20% year 1), working-capital capture (-8%; 9M-2026 operating cash flow of 1.8B against 2.9B of earnings plus D&A confirms growth consumes cash), 2% long-run growth, and the 30/45/25 weights are also unchanged. KNOWN LIMITS: EBITDA includes equity-method earnings (Wilmar and others, 388M in 9M-2026) that convert to cash only as dividends; the 30 Sep balance sheet already reflects nine months of the year-1 flow, a small overlap inherent in the FY0 convention. Revenue for FY2022-FY2025 uses the us-gaap:Revenues total (see ADM_Corrections.jsonl).
inputs.share_count_basis: Weighted-average diluted shares, Q3 2026 10-Q (484M; basic and diluted coincide). Held FLAT because SBC is expensed in the flows. Repurchaser: $358M bought back in 9M-2026 after none in FY2025, so the flat count is being funded.
inputs.net_debt_basis: Q3 2026 10-Q balance sheet (30 Sep 2026): short-term debt 1,156 + current maturities 153 + long-term debt 7,429 = 8,738; less cash 711 and short-term marketable securities 45 = 756. The prior build used 7,604 of debt, which was long-term debt only and omitted short-term borrowings (commercial paper); that omission is corrected here.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Revenue and EPS CAGRs (both computed on the SEC-XBRL-corrected series, see inputs.notes) diverge sharply from equity CAGR and from each other -- revenue fell -7.5% p.a. over 3yr and EPS fell -30.7% p.a. over 3yr purely because FY2022 was a crush-margin/commodity-price peak (EPS $7.71) and FY2025 a trough (EPS $2.23), with owner-FCF also swinging from -9.9% margin (FY2019) to +6.2% (FY2021). None of these historical CAGRs are used as the forward growth driver -- a flat ~2% volume-growth assumption is used instead, per inputs.notes, because this is a mature scale commodity processor whose revenue is overwhelmingly a function of ag commodity prices, not a compounding growth trajectory. Equity CAGR (2.6%) is the most representative growth proxy of the three and is used only as the historical-growth disclosure, not literally as the projected revenue growth rate.

base.narrative: Year 1 is FY2026 at guidance: revenue up about 7.8% (price-led) and a 5.9% EBITDA margin, about 5.1B, consistent with 3.81B of adjusted EBITDA in nine months and adjusted EPS of 5.50-5.80. From there the upswing fades as management itself expects: revenue flat in year 2 as oil and oilseed prices stop rising, then 2% volume-like growth, with the margin stepping down 5.4, 5.2, 5.1 to a 5.0% through-cycle level (about 4.6B of EBITDA by year 5, a little under the FY2021-FY2026 average of roughly 4.9B). Capex returns from the trimmed FY2026 budget to about 1.5% of revenue, SBC normalises from a performance-inflated 0.23% to 0.15%, cash tax ramps 20 to 23%, and growth consumes working capital at 8% of the revenue change.

bull.narrative: The record 2026-2027 RVOs and the 45Z credit prove durable, crush debottlenecking delivers at a quarter of greenfield capital intensity, Carbohydrate Solutions keeps its ethanol and Vantage gains, and Nutrition resumes the recovery that stalled in Q3. FY2026 lands at the top of guidance (6.0% margin) and the margin holds near 6% for four more years before easing to 5.8%, i.e. a through-cycle level close to FY2021-FY2023 rather than a return to FY2024-FY2025.

bear.narrative: FY2026 still lands at the low end of guidance, because nine months are already reported, and then the cycle turns: management was right that margins peaked, RVOs or 45Z are trimmed or challenged, soybean oil prices fall (revenue down 4% in year 2) and the EBITDA margin drops to 4.3% then sits at 3.8-4.0%, the FY2024-FY2025 trough, for the rest of the horizon. Human Nutrition keeps shrinking and capex cannot be cut below maintenance.

scenario_narratives.base: FY2026 lands at guidance (about 5.1B EBITDA), then margins mean-revert to a 5.0% through-cycle level on a revenue base that stops inflating; neither the FY2026 upswing nor the FY2025 trough is capitalised.
scenario_narratives.bull: Biofuel policy holds, debottlenecking and ethanol gains stick, Nutrition recovers: margin stays near 6% and settles at 5.8%.
scenario_narratives.bear: Margins peaked in Q3 2026: policy support erodes, prices fall, and EBITDA margin returns to the 3.8-4.0% trough and stays there.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Unchanged at 30/45/25. Bear stays at 30%, double the house default, because a growing share of profit rests on RVOs and the 45Z credit, both politically reversible, and the CEO said on the Q3 call that crush and biofuel margins may have peaked, with no FY2027 guidance given. Base 45%: mean reversion from a guided peak is the central expectation for this business. Bull held at 25% because it needs durable policy, sustained crush strength and a Nutrition recovery at once, and Q3 Nutrition growth slowed to 3%. The SEC matter settling in January 2026 removes one bear argument from the prior rationale; the peak comment replaces it.

valuation_philosophy.summary: ADM is a thin-margin, highly cyclical agricultural processor whose earnings swing three to four times through the crush and biofuel-policy cycle (EPS 7.71 in FY2022, 2.23 in FY2025, about 5.65 guided for FY2026). The valuation takes FY2026 as it is being delivered, then normalises to a 5.0% through-cycle EBITDA margin over four years, with scenarios spanning a 5.8% and a 4.0% steady state. Risk is carried in those flows and in a 30% bear weight, not in the discount rate, which is 8.7% in every scenario. Terminal value is capped at 12x terminal owner FCF, the low end of the cyclical range and under 6x EBITDA. Net debt includes short-term borrowings.
key_risks_to_valuation: Biofuel policy reversal (RVO cut, 45Z repeal or legal challenge) removes a large share of FY2026-FY2027 profit; management has already said margins may have peaked

Terminal value is bound by the 12x cap in every scenario; each turn of the cap is worth roughly 1.7 per share in the base case, and the market currently pays a much higher multiple of mid-cycle FCF than the model does
Through-cycle margin is a judgment between a 3.8% trough and a 6.5% peak; 0.5pp of EBITDA margin is roughly 450M a year
Net debt of about 8.0B including commercial paper swings with inventory values; a quarter-end balance can differ by 1B or more from the average
EBITDA includes equity-method earnings (Wilmar) that reach ADM only as dividends
Nutrition recovery is inconsistent (Human Nutrition down in Q3 2026) and shareholder litigation from the 2024 accounting matter continues
